note: Loader arguments for the captures that cannot be opened from their own
contents. A capture in this file stores a cycle count and nothing else that
a recovery needs: no key, or no plaintexts and no seed, because the capture
script held one or both as a module constant. archive.load then raises, and
the cell reads as unreproducible for a reason that has nothing to do with
the part.
This is a LOCAL OVERLAY and not derived. tools/make_cells.py folds it into
cells.json where the upstream block carries no key or seed of its own, and
marks the cell so a reader can see where the value came from. It is a file
here rather than a constant in reproduce.py because it is data about
particular captures, and because an earlier revision of the research tree
carried these as `key_hex` and `pt_seed` on the blocks themselves and a
later merge dropped them: a value that lives in only one tree disappears
when that tree is regenerated.
WHY SUPPLYING A KEY IS NOT ASSUMING THE ANSWER. The recovery never reads
the key: it recovers the round-10 subkey from ciphertexts and timings, and
the key is used afterwards, to score the result and to check that inverting
the schedule gives the key back. A wrong key therefore produces a clean
0/16 and not a wrong 16/16, so a row that reports `16/16 verified` has
proved the key it was given. On the JSON captures there is a second and
stronger check: each file's header carries the device's own self-test
ciphertext for the all-zero block, and reproduce.py refuses the capture if
the key does not reproduce it.
seed_note: 12648430 is 0xC0FFEE, the seed constant the capture scripts on this bench use; the firmware's xorshift32 and flashattack.transport.gen_pts are byte-for-byte mirrors of each other, so the plaintexts regenerate exactly.

results/stm32l152/l152re_32mhz.npz.why: one cycle array per (layout, FLASH_ACR) cell named cy_<lay>_<acr>, plus the PRNG seed. No key, no plaintexts and no ciphertexts: every capture in this campaign predates the archive loader.

results/g4_ctguard/g4ct_map.npz.why: the FLASH_ACR x code-offset map: one cycle array per cell, named cy_flash_<acr>. Neither the key nor the seed is a field; both were constants in the capture script.

results/g4_ctguard/g4ct_codepad.npz.why: the CODEPAD sweep, same campaign and same shape as g4ct_map.npz. Its cells are flat, so only the distinct count is read, but the arguments are here so a block on one of them does not need a second lookup.

results/stm32g474/g4_align_sweep.npz.why: the table-alignment sweep: one array per (code offset, FLASH_ACR) named o<off>_<acr> and nothing else at all, not even a rows string.

results/stm32l552/l5_surface.npz.why: the ICACHE x line-offset surface, one array per cell named cyc_<waysel>_<off>, plus two summary strings.

results/mpc5606b/aes_sbox_flash_20k_2026.why: a JSON capture with no key field. The header's self-test ciphertext for the all-zero block is what confirms it.

results/mpc5606b/aes_ttable1_flash_20260.why: same campaign, the compact single-table build.

results/mpc5606b/aes_sbox_dflash2_202609.why: same campaign, tables in the DFLASH array.
